language_instruction: **Source language:** Classical (literary) Mongolian in the traditional Uighur-Mongol vertical script, printed from woodblocks (Beijing Kanjur, 1718–20). It is NOT Manchu. Columns run top to bottom and are read from LEFT to RIGHT. Transcribe in Mongolian script (Unicode U+1800 block), one source column per line, in reading order. The margin carries a Chinese section/volume/folio label. Report the primary language in the <language> tag.

<meta>Beijing Kanjur (1718–1720), Vinaya (Dulba) section, Volume 6 (ča), Folio 3a (recto); red woodblock print in pothi format, 25 vertical columns read left to right.</meta>

<margin>ᠴᠠ ᠳ᠋ᠤᠯᠪᠠ ᠭᠤᠷᠪᠠᠨ ᠳ᠋ᠡᠭᠡᠳᠦ</margin>
<margin>律師戒行經第六卷上三</margin>
ᠪᠢᠰᠢᠷᠡᠯ ᠢᠶᠡᠨ ᠃ ᠰᠠᠢᠨ ᠤ ᠠᠴᠢ ᠪᠠᠷ ᠬᠤᠪᠢᠯᠭᠠᠨ ᠢ ᠦᠵᠡᠭᠦᠯᠦᠭᠡᠳ ᠦᠢᠯᠡᠳᠦᠭᠰᠡᠨ
ᠴᠢᠨᠠᠷ ᠢ ᠦᠵᠡᠭᠦᠯᠵᠦ ᠃ ᠠᠮᠢᠲᠠᠨ ᠢ ᠪᠣᠯᠪᠠᠰᠤᠷᠠᠭᠤᠯᠤᠭᠠᠳ ᠦᠢᠯᠡᠳᠪᠡᠢ ᠅ ᠲᠡᠨᠳᠡ ᠠᠴᠠ ᠪᠠᠰᠠ ᠰᠣᠨᠣᠰᠤᠭᠠᠳ
ᠢᠯᠠᠵᠤ ᠲᠡᠭᠦᠰ ᠨᠦᠭᠴᠢᠭᠰᠡᠨ ᠃ ᠲᠡᠭᠦᠨ ᠳᠦ ᠢᠯᠡᠳᠲᠡ ᠦᠵᠡᠭᠦᠯᠦᠨ
ᠪᠣᠯᠪᠠᠰᠤ ᠬᠠᠮᠤᠭ ᠨᠣᠮ ᠤᠨ ᠃ ᠰᠠᠢᠲᠤᠷ ᠨᠣᠮᠯᠠᠭᠰᠠᠨ ᠳᠤ ᠪᠣᠯᠪᠠᠢ
ᠨᠢᠭᠡᠨ ᠴᠠᠭ ᠲᠤ ᠃ ᠪᠤᠷᠬᠠᠨ ᠬᠠᠮᠤᠭ ᠠᠶᠠᠭ ᠬᠠ ᠲᠡᠭᠢᠮᠯᠢᠭ ᠦᠳ
ᠪᠣᠯᠪᠠᠢ ᠬᠡᠮᠡᠪᠡᠢ ᠅ ᠲᠡᠨᠳᠡ ᠠᠴᠠ ᠠᠶᠠᠭ ᠬᠠ ᠲᠡᠭᠢᠮᠯᠢᠭ ᠦᠳ ᠲᠦ ᠡᠨᠡ
ᠢᠷᠡᠵᠦ ᠢᠯᠠᠵᠤ ᠲᠡᠭᠦᠰ ᠃ ᠨᠦᠭᠴᠢᠭᠰᠡᠨ ᠦ ᠵᠠᠷᠯᠢᠭ ᠢ ᠰᠣᠨᠣᠰᠴᠤ
ᠵᠠᠷᠯᠢᠭ ᠪᠣᠯᠤᠭᠰᠠᠨ ᠢ ᠂ ᠠᠶᠠᠭ ᠬᠠ ᠲᠡᠭᠢᠮᠯᠢᠭ ᠦᠳ ᠰᠣᠨᠣᠰᠤᠭᠠᠳ ᠂
ᠦᠨᠡᠬᠡᠷ ᠪᠠᠶᠠᠰᠴᠤ ᠅ ᠲᠡᠨᠳᠡ ᠠᠴᠠ ᠪᠠᠰᠠ ᠠᠶᠠᠭ ᠬᠠ ᠲᠡᠭᠢᠮᠯᠢᠭ
ᠦᠢᠯᠡ ᠶᠢ ᠦᠢᠯᠡᠳᠬᠦᠢ ᠳᠦ ᠂ ᠢᠯᠠᠵᠤ ᠲᠡᠭᠦᠰ ᠨᠦᠭᠴᠢᠭᠰᠡᠨ
ᠵᠠᠷᠯᠢᠭ ᠪᠣᠯᠪᠠᠢ ᠅ ᠠᠶᠠᠭ ᠬᠠ ᠲᠡᠭᠢᠮᠯᠢᠭ ᠦᠳ ᠠᠴᠠ ᠠᠯᠢ ᠪᠠ
ᠰᠠᠬᠢᠯ ᠢ ᠠᠯᠳᠠᠭᠰᠠᠨ ᠃ ᠪᠤᠰᠤᠳ ᠠᠶᠠᠭ ᠬᠠ ᠲᠡᠭᠢᠮᠯᠢᠭ
 ᠦᠳ ᠲᠦ ᠂ ᠬᠡᠷᠪᠡ ᠲᠡᠷᠡ ᠠᠶᠠᠭ ᠬᠠ ᠲᠡᠭᠢᠮᠯᠢᠭ ᠢ ᠦᠵᠡᠭᠡᠳ ᠅
ᠴᠢᠨᠠᠭᠰᠢ ᠪᠣᠯᠤᠭᠰᠠᠨ ᠢ ᠂ ᠮᠡᠳᠡᠭᠡᠳ ᠨᠣᠮ ᠤᠨ ᠶᠣᠰᠤᠭᠠᠷ
ᠦᠢᠯᠡᠳᠬᠦ ᠪᠣᠯᠪᠠᠰᠤ ᠂ ᠲᠡᠷᠡ ᠠᠶᠠᠭ ᠬᠠ ᠲᠡᠭᠢᠮᠯᠢᠭ ᠢ
ᠨᠠᠮᠠᠨᠴᠢᠯᠠᠭᠤᠯᠵᠤ ᠂ ᠭᠡᠮ ᠠᠴᠠ ᠭᠠᠷᠭᠠᠬᠤ ᠪᠣᠯᠤᠮᠤᠢ ᠅
ᠬᠡᠷᠪᠡ ᠲᠡᠢᠮᠦ ᠪᠣᠯᠪᠠᠰᠤ ᠂ ᠠᠶᠠᠭ ᠬᠠ ᠲᠡᠭᠢᠮᠯᠢᠭ ᠦᠳ
ᠰᠠᠢᠲᠤᠷ ᠰᠢᠨᠵᠢᠯᠡᠵᠦ ᠂ ᠨᠣᠮ ᠤᠨ ᠶᠣᠰᠤᠭᠠᠷ ᠦᠢᠯᠡᠳᠬᠦ
ᠪᠣᠯᠲᠤᠭᠠᠢ ᠬᠡᠮᠡᠪᠡᠢ ᠂ ᠅
ᠪᠠᠰᠠ ᠢᠯᠠᠵᠤ ᠲᠡᠭᠦᠰ ᠨᠦᠭᠴᠢᠭᠰᠡᠨ ᠳᠦ ᠂
ᠨᠠᠰᠤᠨ ᠠᠴᠠ ᠲᠡᠭᠦᠯᠳᠡᠷ ᠤᠫᠠᠯᠢ ᠡᠶᠢᠨ ᠬᠡᠮᠡᠨ ᠦᠴᠢᠪᠡᠢ ᠃
ᠢᠯᠠᠵᠤ ᠲᠡᠭᠦᠰ ᠨᠦᠭᠴᠢᠭᠰᠡᠨ ᠠ ᠂ ᠠᠶᠠᠭ ᠬᠠ ᠲᠡᠭᠢᠮᠯᠢᠭ ᠦᠳ
ᠴᠢᠨᠠᠭᠰᠢ ᠂ ᠰᠠᠬᠢᠯ ᠠᠴᠠ ᠠᠯᠳᠠᠭᠰᠠᠨ ᠢ ᠦᠵᠡᠪᠡᠰᠦ
ᠬᠡᠷ ᠦᠢᠯᠡᠳᠬᠦ ᠪᠣᠯᠤᠮᠤᠢ ᠬᠡᠮᠡᠨ ᠦᠴᠢᠭᠰᠡᠨ ᠳᠦ ᠃
ᠢᠯᠠᠵᠤ ᠲᠡᠭᠦᠰ ᠨᠦᠭᠴᠢᠭᠰᠡᠨ ᠨᠠᠰᠤᠨ ᠠᠴᠠ ᠲᠡᠭᠦᠯᠳᠡᠷ ᠤᠫᠠᠯᠢ ᠳᠤ ᠵᠠᠷᠯᠢᠭ ᠃

<vocab>ᠳ᠋ᠤᠯᠪᠠ (Dulba / Vinaya), ᠢᠯᠠᠵᠤ ᠲᠡᠭᠦᠰ ᠨᠦᠭᠴᠢᠭᠰᠡᠨ (ilaju tegüs nögčigsen / Bhagavān), ᠠᠶᠠᠭ ᠬᠠ ᠲᠡᠭᠢᠮᠯᠢᠭ (ayag-qa tegimlig / bhikṣu), ᠨᠠᠰᠤᠨ ᠠᠴᠠ ᠲᠡᠭᠦᠯᠳᠡᠷ ᠤᠫᠠᠯᠢ (nasun-ača tegülder Upali / Āyuṣmat Upāli), ᠰᠠᠬᠢᠯ (sakil / śīla), 律師戒行經 (Lǜshī jièxíng jīng)</vocab>

<meta>continues from previous page</meta>
<meta>Beijing Kanjur, 1718 to 1720, Vinaya or Dulba section, Volume 6, ča, Folio 3a recto; red woodblock print in pothi format, 25 vertical columns read left to right.</meta>

<margin>Volume <term>Ča</term> <gloss>the sixth volume letter in the Tibetan and Mongolian canonical sequence</gloss>, <term>Dulba</term> <gloss>Monastic Discipline, corresponding to the Sanskrit Vinaya</gloss>, Folio Three, Upper <note>original: "ča dulba gurban degedü", indicating Volume 6, Folio 3a recto</note></margin>
<margin><term>Lǜshī jièxíng jīng</term> <gloss>Scripture on the Precepts and Conduct of Vinaya Masters</gloss>, Volume Six, Upper Three <note>original: "律師戒行經第六卷上三", the Chinese marginal volume and folio signature used by the Beijing printshop</note></margin>
their devotion. Through the grace of wholesome merit, having displayed miraculous transformations and revealed the true nature of what had been enacted,
he brought sentient beings to spiritual maturity. Thereafter, having also heard this,
the Victoriously Transcendent One, the <term>Bhagavān</term> <gloss>Blessed Lord, standard Buddhist epithet rendered in Mongolian as ilaju tegüs nögčigsen</gloss>, clearly demonstrating this to them,
brought it about that all elements of the <term>Dharma</term> <gloss>the Buddhist teaching and law; Mongolian nom</gloss> were well expounded.
At one time, the Buddha and all the <term>bhikṣus</term> <gloss>fully ordained Buddhist monks; Mongolian ayaγ-qa tegimlig, literally "worthy of reverence"</gloss>
were gathered together, so it is said. Then, having come before the monks and listened to the pronouncement of the Victoriously Transcendent One,
when the monks heard what had been proclaimed,
they truly rejoiced. Thereafter, moreover, when the monks
were performing the formal ecclesiastical acts, the Victoriously Transcendent One
spoke thus: "If any among the monks
has transgressed a <term>sakil</term> <gloss>monastic precept or vow, translating Sanskrit śīla</gloss>, and with respect to the other monks,
if those monks observe that monk
and know that he has gone beyond bounds into transgression, and if they act in accordance with the law of the teaching,
they shall cause that monk
to make formal confession and thereby release him from the offense.
If such a case arises, the monks
should examine the matter thoroughly and act in accordance with the law of the teaching."
So he spoke.
Furthermore, to the Victoriously Transcendent One,
the Venerable <term>Āyuṣmat Upāli</term> <gloss>the foremost disciple of the Buddha in monastic discipline; rendered in Mongolian as nasun-ača tegülder Upali, "Upāli Possessed of Long Life"</gloss> respectfully addressed these words:
"O Victoriously Transcendent One, if the monks
subsequently observe someone who has fallen away from a precept,
how should they proceed?" When he had thus inquired,
the Victoriously Transcendent One addressed his word to the Venerable Upāli <note>the sentence concludes on the following page, Folio 3b</note>

<summary>This folio from the sixth volume of the Vinaya section of the Beijing Mongolian Kanjur records the Buddha's instructions on communal monastic procedure when a monk transgresses a precept. The Buddha directs the community to investigate offenses according to monastic law and restore the offender through formal confession, followed by a query from the disciple Upāli on how monks should handle observed breaches of discipline.</summary>
<keywords>Beijing Kanjur, Classical Mongolian, Vinaya, Dulba, monastic discipline, Bhagavān, bhikṣu, Upāli, precepts, śīla, confession, ecclesiastical procedure</keywords>
